elements.element: Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it
elements.evidence: "all right, title and interest in and to the design, look and feel, and other materials and work product developed specifically for the Company or the Site under this Agreement (the \"Deliverables\")"

elements.element: Vendor effects a present assignment of those deliverables to Customer
elements.evidence: "HDI hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest in and to ... the Deliverables"
"excluding HDI's pre-existing and generally applicable software, systems, tools and know-how, which HDI retains"

elements.element: Licence to Customer of Vendor IP embedded in deliverables
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense the same to the extent embedded in or reasonably necessary to use the Deliverables"

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data
elements.evidence: "the Company owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to ... all customer, user, order and transaction data collected through or generated by the Site ... (the \"Company Data\")"
"no joint ownership of any of the foregoing is created"

elements.element: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how
elements.evidence: "generally applicable software, systems, tools and know-how, which HDI retains"

elements.element: Customer receives perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business
elements.evidence: Customer is assigned the Deliverables outright and holds a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense" the embedded Vendor IP

reasons: The document was silent on proprietary rights, so a single concise inserted Section 5.5 is a proportionate remedy rather than a rewrite.

All preferred atomic elements are expressly present: Vendor assignment of Deliverables, Vendor retention of pre-existing IP, a perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free embedded-IP licence, Customer ownership of Content, Marks and Company Data, and an express no-joint-ownership statement.
The 'worldwide' and 'use, modify and sublicense' scope words are necessary operative content of any embedded-IP licence grant, not surplus protection, so minimality is preserved.

No unrelated term is disturbed: Sections 2.1, 5.2, the trademark licence sentence and 7.1 remain untouched and effective, and defined terms ('Content', 'Marks', 'Deerskin Products') are used consistently with the Agreement, with 'Company Data' newly defined in place.
